text:
Jordan's week pivots on a single referral that arrived on the 9th and, within two days, turned into real momentum. Lena texted the application in — product designer at Northlight, under Ana — and the door that had been theoretical since July suddenly had a handle on it. What's notable is what happened next: Jordan sat down expecting the portfolio update to be the hard part, the thing dreaded since July, and found it wasn't. The Meridian case studies held up. The real work was finally writing up Coda honestly, including the part that had stung — Dev repurposing the free-play mode as a bug tracker on a Thursday, after Jordan had dogfooded it daily for nine days without seeing what it actually was. Writing that up straight, instead of smoothing it into a success story, turned it into the strongest piece in the portfolio. Jordan notes, almost wryly, that Mika said "maybe Coda IS the portfolio update" back on July 31st, and Lena said something similar on the 14th, and it took actually doing the work to believe either of them.

The submission went in at 11:20pm on the 9th, with a cover letter that skipped the pretend-enthusiasm move — a small but deliberate choice.

Two days later, the phone screen with Ana confirmed the bet. Jordan chose honesty again under pressure: telling Ana the dashboard project failed twice because Jordan was designing to a moving target (Marcus, unnamed but clearly implied), and only worked once Jordan stopped guessing what the manager wanted. Ana's reaction — recognizing the type — landed well. The Coda conversation went deeper than expected, eleven minutes on it, with Ana zeroing in on exactly the detail Jordan had been most honest about: nine days of blindness before seeing the feature clearly. Ana's response — "I wanted to know if you'd pretend you had" — seems to have validated the whole approach of writing the case study without spin. An onsite is now set for roughly two weeks out, full day, four interviews plus a presentation, with Ana naming an October hiring timeline.

The emotional throughline is the shift in scale: the reorg and the looming report-to-Priya date on the 21st haven't changed at all, but the meaning changed overnight from "the whole sky" to "an inconvenience I might be leaving," a reframe Jordan caught in real time on the Greenwood Park hill trail and wanted on record before doubting it later.

Unresolved heading into next week: nothing at work has been said to anyone there — this is still a secret held outside the office, shared instead with Lena, Mika, Dev, and Mom within twenty minutes of the call. The onsite hasn't happened. The October timeline creates pressure. And Jordan's own pattern — bracing for spirals, distrusting good news, needing to see things written down to believe them — is visibly still active, just currently winning.
